cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to Timothy, his true child in the faith (1 Timothy 1:1-2). He's just finished teaching how the church should pray and worship together. Now he hands Timothy a trustworthy saying about anyone who aspires to be an overseer in the church.

cards.question: Paul says anyone who aspires to be an overseer desires a noble task.

cards.text: Then Paul starts a LIST, friend. An overseer must be above reproach, the husband of but one wife, temperate, self-controlled and respectable.

cards.question: Paul's list keeps going. An overseer must be hospitable and able to ___.

cards.text: An overseer must not be dependent on wine, and not violent but gentle and peaceable. I once yelled at an oven timer for a FULL minute, so I'm reading this one twice.

cards.question: An overseer must be gentle and peaceable. What else must he be free of?

cards.text: Next, Paul walks right into the overseer's home life. Friend, this is the part where I'm GLAD I live alone on a cookie planet.

cards.question: An overseer must manage his own ___ well and keep his children under control with complete dignity.
Why does it matter so much how an overseer runs his own household?

answers.text: It shows if he can care for God's church
His family will help him lead the church
The church will gather in his house

cards.text: Then Paul says an overseer must not be a recent convert. You don't hand a brand-new baker the keys to the whole bakery on day one.

cards.question: Paul says a recent convert shouldn't be an overseer because he doesn't know enough Scripture yet.

cards.text: Last item for overseers: he must have a good reputation with outsiders. Paul's not just checking references at church, friend; he's calling the NEIGHBORS.

cards.question: Why does an overseer need a good reputation with people outside the church?

answers.text: So he won't fall into disgrace and the devil's snare
So more outsiders will want to join the church
So the city's rulers will protect the church

cards.text: Now Paul turns to deacons. They must be dignified and not double-tongued, so NO telling somebody "Love the cookies!" and then roasting them in the group chat.

cards.question: Deacons must not be given to much wine or greedy for ___.

cards.text: Deacons must hold to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience. But Paul doesn't just hand them the job.

cards.question: Before anyone serves as a deacon, they must first be ___.

cards.text: Then, if they are above reproach, let them serve as deacons. Same way you run one test batch in a new oven before you trust it with the big order.
In the same way, Paul says, the women must be dignified, temperate and faithful in all things.

cards.question: Paul also names one thing these women must not be. What is it?
Back to deacons. Just like an overseer, a deacon must be the husband of but one wife.

cards.text: A deacon must also be a good manager of his children and his own household. And Paul says those who serve well as deacons walk away with something.

cards.question: What do those who serve well as deacons gain for themselves?

answers.text: High standing and great confidence in the faith
A larger share of the church's offerings
A seat among the overseers of the church

cards.text: Paul hopes to come to Timothy soon, but he's writing these things in case he's delayed. Friend, we've all sent a "running late" text, but Paul sent instructions for the whole CHURCH.

cards.question: Why is Paul writing all this down for Timothy?

answers.text: So he knows how people must act in God's household
So he can read it aloud to the city's rulers
So he can choose who will take Paul's place

cards.text: And what is God's household? Paul says it's the church of the living God.

cards.question: Paul calls the church of the living God the pillar and foundation of the ___.

cards.text: Then Paul ends BIG. By common confession, he says, the mystery of godliness is great: "He appeared in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, was seen by angels" and he's not done yet.

cards.question: Paul says the news about Him stayed a secret shared by only a few.
Paul's list starts with Him appearing in the flesh. Where does the list end?

answers.text: He was taken up in glory
He was laid in a tomb

findings.problem: The opening card states a Bible fact from outside the passage with no reference: "He's just finished teaching how the church should pray and worship together." That fact comes from 1 Timothy 2. The card gives a reference for 1 Timothy 1:1-2 but none for this.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to finish Paul's list ("hospitable and able to ___"). The baker hasn't seen this wording and nothing on the earlier cards lets them reason to "teach" over "travel" or "sing." It's a guess at the next words of a line in a letter.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The joke "this is the part where I'm GLAD I live alone on a cookie planet" plays as relief at having no kids to manage. That clashes with his family facts: he is Papa to six kids he misses and hopes to see again.

rule.text: He misses them and hopes to see them again.

findings.problem: Card 7 says Paul "walks right into the overseer's home life," and the question itself mentions "keep his children under control." Together these give away "household" and rule out "business" and "schedule."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke "You don't hand a brand-new baker the keys to the whole bakery on day one" suggests the reason is inexperience. Verse 6 gives a different reason: he may become conceited and fall under the devil's condemnation. The joke adds a reason the text doesn't give. It also steers the baker toward the wrong answer on card 11, which asks whether the reason is not knowing enough Scripture.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The real reason in 1 Timothy 3:6 (he may become conceited and fall under the same condemnation as the devil) is never told on any card. The true or false only rules out a made-up reason, so the baker leaves without the verse's actual point.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to finish the line "the pillar and foundation of the ___." No earlier card gives anything to reason from, so choosing "truth" over "nations" or "law" is a guess at unseen wording.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
